summary.title: EcoEvoApps: Interactive Apps for Theoretical Models in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
summary.authors: Rosa M Mcguire, Kenji T Hayashi, Xinyi Yan, Marcel Caritá Vaz, Damla Cino Glu, Madeline C Cowen, Alejandra Martínez-Blancas, Lauren L Sullivan, Sheila Vazquez-Morales, Gaurav S Kandlikar
summary.field_subfield: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB) / Educational Technology
summary.executive_summary: This paper introduces EcoEvoApps, an open-source R package and website designed to bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical research in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB). The primary motivation is to address the barrier that mathematical models often present to empiricists, who may find equation-heavy literature intimidating or less accessible. EcoEvoApps provides a collection of 11 interactive Shiny apps that simulate fundamental EEB models, such as predator-prey dynamics, island biogeography, and resource competition. These apps allow users to explore model structures and outcomes by manipulating parameters, thereby fostering a deeper conceptual understanding without requiring extensive coding or analytical skills. The package also includes underlying R functions for simulating and visualizing model dynamics, serving as a gateway for users to transition from interactive exploration to command-line implementation. The authors evaluated the educational utility of these apps in classroom settings at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and the University of Missouri (MU). Surveys of 51 students at UCLA indicated that an overwhelming majority (40/51) found the apps moderately to very helpful for understanding the models. Similar positive results were observed at MU, with notable gains in student confidence, particularly among those with higher initial interest in the topics. The project is designed to be collaborative and inclusive, with apps available in multiple languages including English, Spanish, Chinese, Turkish, and Portuguese. The authors invite community contributions to expand the model library, add new features, and develop teaching plans. By leveraging the R ecosystem, EcoEvoApps offers a customizable, accessible, and open-source alternative to existing educational resources, aiming to facilitate communication and collaboration between theoretical and empirical researchers in the EEB community.

claims.description: Interactive Shiny apps effectively facilitate the understanding of theoretical EEB models in classroom settings.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper introduces EcoEvoApps, an open-source R package and website designed to bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical research in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB). The primary motivation is to address the barrier that mathematical models often present to empiricists, who may find equation-heavy literature intimidating or less accessible. EcoEvoApps provides a collection of 11 interactive Shiny apps that simulate fundamental EEB models, such as predator-prey dynamics, island biogeography, and resource competition. These apps allow users to explore model structures and outcomes by manipulating parameters, thereby fostering a deeper conceptual understanding without requiring extensive coding or analytical skills. The package also includes underlying R functions for simulating and visualizing model dynamics, serving as a gateway for users to transition from interactive exploration to command-line implementation. The authors evaluated the educational utility of these apps in classroom settings at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and the University of Missouri (MU). Surveys of 51 students at UCLA indicated that an overwhelming majority (40/51) found the apps moderately to very helpful for understanding the models. Similar positive results were observed at MU, with notable gains in student confidence, particularly among those with higher initial interest in the topics. The project is designed to be collaborative and inclusive, with apps available in multiple languages including English, Spanish, Chinese, Turkish, and Portuguese. The authors invite community contributions to expand the model library, add new features, and develop teaching plans. By leveraging the R ecosystem, EcoEvoApps offers a customizable, accessible, and open-source alternative to existing educational resources, aiming to facilitate communication and collaboration between theoretical and empirical researchers in the EEB community.

Research Context
Integrating theory with observations is a fundamental driver of progress in life sciences. Mathematical models enable generalization and clarify biological factors. Equation-heavy papers are often cited less frequently. Instructors of quantitative courses often receive worse student evaluations. Previous calls for quantitative training focused on statistics or programming. Interactive tools help increase student interest in quantitative concepts. There is a need for better pedagogy of theoretical models.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to provide a platform for interactive simulations of EEB models. The hypothesis is that interactive apps facilitate communication between theoretical and empirical researchers. The apps are expected to help users gain familiarity with model structure. The package serves as a bridge to coding and implementing theoretical models. The study evaluates the utility of these apps in classroom settings. It is predicted that apps will help students understand specific model topics.

Methodological Details
The core of the package consists of 11 interactive Shiny apps. Models were selected by surveying undergraduate ecology syllabi and textbooks. Apps include descriptions, parameter tables, and literature references. Nine apps are available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Turkish, and Portuguese. Apps are hosted on RStudio's shinyapps.io servers. The package includes functions with the prefix shiny_ for local deployment. Simulations are conducted by functions with the prefix run_. Plotting functions are prefixed with plot_ and return ggplot2 objects. A classroom survey was conducted with 51 students at UCLA. The survey used a scale of 1-7 to rate helpfulness. Similar surveys were conducted at the University of Missouri.

Procedures And Architectures
The package is an open-source R package named ecoevoapps. The website is hosted at https://ecoevoapps.gitlab.io. The predator-prey app includes tabs for Lotka-Volterra and extensions. Extensions include logistic growth and type II functional response. The run_predprey_model() function takes params, init, and time as inputs. The function returns a dataframe of population sizes over time. Users can customize and deploy their own app instances. Model-specific vignettes provide instructions for simulating dynamics in R. The package can be installed from GitLab. The project invites contributions for new apps and translations.

Key Results
An overwhelming majority of students (40/51) found the apps helpful. Students rated the apps as moderately to very helpful (6 or 7). Students reported better understanding of concepts like carrying capacity. Similar results were found in surveys at the University of Missouri. Using interactive apps led to substantial gains in student confidence. Confidence gains were especially high among students with higher interest. The paradox of enrichment can be visualized by altering carrying capacity. Low carrying capacity results in stable oscillations or equilibrium. High carrying capacity results in unstable oscillations.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Interactive tools help disentangle complex interactions and feedbacks. The apps bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical researchers. Simulation-based learning provides easier access to theoretical insights. The open-source nature allows for community customization and expansion. The project aims to complement existing educational web resources. Future work will prioritize evolutionary biology and population genetics models.

Contradictions And Limitations
Simulation-based learning may not provide all insights of analytical solutions. The current release focuses primarily on ecological models. The study relies on self-reported student surveys for efficacy. The sample size for the primary survey was 51 students. The package is in its first release and expected to grow.

Claims
Interactive Shiny apps effectively facilitate the understanding of theoretical EEB models in classroom settings. 40 out of 51 students rated the apps as helpful. Students reported improved understanding of specific concepts. Confidence in models increased after using the apps. Simulation may not replace analytical solutions entirely. Educators can use these apps to teach quantitative models. The apps lower the barrier to entry for theoretical models.

Data And Code Availability
The package is available as an open-source R package. The website is hosted on GitLab. Apps are available on RStudio's shinyapps.io.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The package includes functions for simulating and visualizing dynamics. Users can customize app instances for specific lessons.

Ethical Considerations
Classroom surveys were reviewed by UCLA and MU IRBs. The studies were determined to constitute exempt studies.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the predator-prey dynamics app with model extensions. Figure 2 illustrates the paradox of enrichment with varying K. Figure 3 presents survey results on student helpfulness ratings. Table 1 lists the models and functions included in the package.

Three Takeaways
1. EcoEvoApps provides interactive Shiny apps for fundamental EEB models. 2. Classroom surveys show high student satisfaction and improved understanding. 3. The open-source R package invites community contributions for expansion.
